threeModes.label: DAST · SAST · PR auto-analysis, all in one

benchmark.title: We verified the Java analysis path on the live site
benchmark.sub: We connected the frontend, backend, Java analysis server, Joern, and Qwen and checked both vulnerable and safe examples.

card1.title: Vulnerable and safe examples checked together
card1.desc: The vulnerable Java example produced CWE-79 at the original line, while the safe example produced no finding.
card1.footnote: * This is a two-file functional demonstration, not evidence of detection superiority.

card2.title: Java-specific ensemble analysis
card2.desc: We preserve results and evidence from different analysis methods and merge them into one report.
card2.footer: Java semantic review sends the required code context to the DashScope Qwen API.

why.title: Separate analysis paths for each language and purpose
why.sub: Java combines graph evidence with semantic review, while other languages keep their existing analysis path.

localModel.title: Java CPG + Qwen ensemble
localModel.desc: Joern finds static data flows and Qwen3.8-Max separately reviews code semantics. Reports retain the source and evidence for each finding.

wholeRepo.title: Repository-level Java CPG analysis
wholeRepo.desc: Submitted Java files are passed to Joern as one job to inspect code structure and data flow. Results preserve the original file and line.

confidentFilter.title: Incomplete analysis is reported as failure
confidentFilter.desc: Connection failures, missing files, timeouts, and PARTIAL results are not converted into a safe verdict. A failure state tells users when to retry.

security.title: A transparent path for handling code
security.sub: URL scans require no source code, while repository and PR scans process code through the ScanOps analysis path.

flow1.title: URL scan — no code transfer
steps: ScanOps runs a dynamic scan from the outside
Only a vulnerability report is generated
flow1.note: Your source code itself is never sent to our servers.

flow2.title: Repo and PR scan — ScanOps analysis path
steps: Read the selected code from GitHub
Route it to the language-specific engine
Store findings and evidence in the report
flow2.note: Java semantic review sends the required code context to the external DashScope Qwen API.

memoryOnly.title: Result-focused storage
memoryOnly.desc: The DB stores vulnerability results and report metadata

immediateDeletion.title: Temporary workspace cleanup
immediateDeletion.desc: Joern removes temporary analysis files after each job

readOnly.title: Read-only access
readOnly.desc: Requests only the minimum required GitHub scope

httpsEncryption.title: Protected communication paths
httpsEncryption.desc: Public traffic uses HTTPS; the analysis server is private-VPC only

scanModes.title: From web to repo to PR, all in one
scanModes.sub: Choose the mode that fits what you're scanning. Usage is tracked transparently for each mode.

dast.title: Website dynamic analysis
dast.desc: Scans your running app from the outside. Diagnoses with just a URL — no code transfer required.

sast.title: Full-repo static analysis
sast.desc: Java combines Joern CPG with Qwen3.8-Max, while other languages use the existing analysis engine.

actions.title: Automatic PR analysis
actions.desc: The GitHub App sends changed PR code through the ScanOps analysis path and reports findings on the relevant lines.
